items.q: A 55-year-old man undergoes TIPS and the operator punctures from the right hepatic vein toward the right portal branch. Wedge contrast had outlined the target. Which access-route logic best explains right-vein to right-portal puncture as the standard path?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Straightest run with wedge-mapped targets.** Right-to-right alignment minimises needle angulation while wedge puffs mark portal branches.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Tortuosity complicates punctures
- C: Left routes angle sharply
- D: Maps guide needles truly
**Key point:** Right hepatic to right portal punctures standard.
items.kp: Standard TIPS punctures right hepatic to right portal.

items.q: A 60-year-old woman has a portosystemic gradient of 22 mmHg before TIPS with active bleeding. After tract opening the gradient reads 8 mmHg with bleeding stopped. Which gradient-target logic best explains aiming below twelve millimetres of mercury?
o: Bleeding and ascites ease once gradients fall below twelve
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Bleeding and ascites ease once gradients fall below twelve.** Baveno consensus ties sub-twelve gradients to bleeding control and ascites relief.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: High gradients drive bleeding
- C: Numbers set dilatation endpoints
- D: Twenty sustains bleeding
**Key point:** TIPS targets gradients below twelve.
items.kp: TIPS dilatation targets gradients below twelve millimetres of mercury.

items.q: A 52-year-old man receives a covered stent-graft across his TIPS tract rather than bare metal. The operator cites patency evidence. Which graft logic best explains covered stent-grafts cutting shunt dysfunction?
o: Fabric lining blocks bile and tissue ingrowth through mesh
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Fabric lining blocks bile and tissue ingrowth through mesh.** Covered walls seal bile leaks and bar hyperplasia that choke bare struts.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Fabric prevents rather than causes clots
- C: Bare metal stenoses commonly
- D: Grafts persist rather than dissolve
**Key point:** Covered grafts resist shunt dysfunction.
items.kp: TIPS tracts take covered stent-grafts over bare metal.

items.q: A 64-year-old woman has large gastric varices with a gastrorenal shunt seen alongside portal hypertension. TIPS alone may leave the shunt bleeding. Which combined logic best pairs shunt placement with variceal coil closure?
o: Lower pressure with direct closure of bleeding varices
Shunts always still every varix alone
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Lower pressure with direct closure of bleeding varices.** Big shunts steal flow where varices persist, so coils shut the bleeding channel directly.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Shunts miss some varices
- C: Coils close varices directly
- D: Gastric varices bleed massively
**Key point:** Big varices coil alongside TIPS.
items.kp: Large varices need coils alongside TIPS.

items.q: A 58-year-old man has contrast spilling outside the liver capsule with falling pressure during TIPS puncture. The operator extends a covered stent across the breach. Which capsular-breach logic best rescues transgression with covered extension?
o: Seal the liver hole from inside while restoring tract flow
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Seal the liver hole from inside while restoring tract flow.** Covered grafts bridge capsular tears, tamponading bleeding while completing the shunt.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Watched breaches bleed out
- C: Wires maintain rescue access
- D: Transfusion needs sealing too
**Key point:** Capsular breaches seal with covered extension.
items.kp: Capsular transgression seals with covered-stent extension.

items.q: A 57-year-old woman spikes fevers with right upper quadrant pain a week after TIPS. Imaging shows a crossed bile duct fistula. Which biliary-crossing logic best manages fistulae with antibiotics and drainage?
o: Drain infected bile while antibiotics clear tract seeding
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Drain infected bile while antibiotics clear tract seeding.** Crossed ducts leak germs into tracts where drainage removes pus and drugs clear seeding.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Fevers warn of seeding
- C: Undrained pus spreads
- D: Bile seeds tracts readily
**Key point:** Biliary fistulae drain with antibiotics.
items.kp: Post-TIPS biliary fistulae need drainage with antibiotics.

items.q: A 62-year-old man has his TIPS duplex showing sluggish shunt velocity with hepatofugal portal flow reversed back toward normal. His ascites returns. Which surveillance logic best reads falling velocity with returning ascites as stenosis?
o: Slowing shunts with returning pressure signs mark tract narrowing
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Slowing shunts with returning pressure signs mark tract narrowing.** Stenosis throttles flow where pressure climbs back, and venography with revision follows.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Slow means stenosed
- C: Ascites mirrors gradients
- D: Duplex triggers revision
**Key point:** Falling velocity with ascites means stenosis.
items.kp: Falling shunt velocity with ascites marks stenosis.

items.q: A 49-year-old woman re-bleeds from varices six months after TIPS. Venography shows a widely patent shunt with unchanged gradient. Which failure-site logic best separates patent shunts from persistent varices in re-bleeders?
o: Patent shunts shift blame to untreated variceal channels
Patent shunts always stop all bleeding
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Patent shunts shift blame to untreated variceal channels.** Open shunts with controlled gradients leave varices themselves as culprits needing coils.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Patent misses some varices
- C: Re-mapping finds channels
- D: Varices persist sometimes
**Key point:** Patent-shunt re-bleeds target varices.
items.kp: Re-bleeds with patent shunts need variceal re-mapping.

items.q: A 66-year-old man has Budd-Chiari with no accessible hepatic vein for standard puncture. The operator uses a caudate lobe vein as the entry. Which rescue-route logic best explains caudate access when hepatic veins block?
o: Caudate veins drain separately into cava staying open
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Caudate veins drain separately into cava staying open.** Caudate drainage survives hepatic vein thrombosis, offering a back-door entry to cava.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Caudate reaches cava directly
- C: Blocks reroute rather than forbid
- D: Cava accepts direct sticks
**Key point:** Blocked hepatic veins reroute via caudate.
items.kp: Budd-Chiari without hepatic veins uses caudate access.

items.q: A 53-year-old woman has an arterial blush alongside her TIPS tract with falling haemoglobin. The operator coils the hepatic arterial branch. Which alongside-injury logic best coils arterial blushes beside new tracts?
o: Tract needles nick arteries that coils then close
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Tract needles nick arteries that coils then close.** Stiff needles cross arterial twigs beside veins where coils seal the nick precisely.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Blushes bleed on unwatched
- C: Needles cross arteries
- D: Haemoglobin guides rescue
**Key point:** Tract arterial nicks coil shut.
items.kp: Arterial blushes beside TIPS tracts need coils.

items.q: A 56-year-old man has his TIPS stent landing short in the portal vein with the lower end floating in parenchyma. Flow looks sluggish. Which malposition logic best explains extending short stents fully into portal veins?
o: Uncovered gaps clot where blood meets bare tract
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Uncovered gaps clot where blood meets bare tract.** Bare parenchymal gaps invite thrombosis where covered metal should line the full channel.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Short leaves clot-prone gaps
- C: Parenchyma bleeds not grips
- D: Landings govern flow
**Key point:** Short TIPS stents extend into portal veins.
items.kp: Short TIPS landings extend fully into portal veins.

items.q: A 61-year-old woman has her stent tip reaching the right atrium with ectopics on the monitor. Cardiology stands by. Which atrial-malposition logic best manages stents reaching too far into hearts?
o: Pull back under cardiac watching before arrhythmias worsen
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Pull back under cardiac watching before arrhythmias worsen.** Atrial metal irritates conduction where repositioning under monitoring prevents arrest.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Deeper worsens arrhythmias
- C: Ectopics warn of irritation
- D: Hearts stay put firmly
**Key point:** Atrial stents pull back watched.
items.kp: Atrial TIPS stents reposition under cardiac watching.

items.q: A 54-year-old man has stepwise balloon dilatation from 6 to 8 to 10 mm with gradient checks between. Bleeding stops at 8 mm so the operator halts. Which stepwise logic best stops dilatation once targets hit?
o: Dilate to effect rather than maximum size
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Dilate to effect rather than maximum size.** Each millimetre trades pressure for encephalopathy where stopping at control preserves brains.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Maximum invites confusion
- C: Gradients set stopping points
- D: Control defines success
**Key point:** TIPS dilatation stops at effect.
items.kp: TIPS balloons stop once gradients and bleeding control.

items.q: A 59-year-old woman has an oversized balloon tear her liver capsule with massive bleeding. The team tamponades with a covered stent. Which oversize lesson best restrains balloons to stepwise sizing?
o: Oversized balloons tear capsules into catastrophe
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Oversized balloons tear capsules into catastrophe.** Parenchyma splits beyond its stretch where covered rescue barely contains the damage.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Bigger tears catastrophically
- C: Capsules split readily
- D: Bleeding needs sealing
**Key point:** Oversized TIPS balloons tear capsules.
items.kp: Oversized balloons tear liver capsules catastrophically.

items.q: A 63-year-old man has his jugular sheath kink with difficult catheter torque during TIPS. The operator swaps to a stiffer sheath with ultrasound-guided re-access. Which sheath-support logic best explains stiff sheaths for torque-heavy TIPS work?
o: Rigid platforms transmit needle force without buckling
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Rigid platforms transmit needle force without buckling.** Colapinto needles need braced guides where floppy sheaths fold and waste force.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Kinks waste needle force
- C: Floppy folds under load
- D: Torque drives punctures
**Key point:** TIPS needs stiff braced sheaths.
items.kp: Torque-heavy TIPS work needs stiff sheaths.

items.q: A 50-year-old woman has CO2 wedged venography instead of iodinated contrast due to severe allergy. The operator maps portal branches with gas. Which allergy-adapted logic best uses CO2 mapping in contrast-allergic TIPS cases?
o: Gas outlines veins without iodinated reactions
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Gas outlines veins without iodinated reactions.** Carbon dioxide bubbles map veins where iodine would trigger anaphylaxis.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Mapping adapts rather than stops
- C: Gas images veins well
- D: Iodine threatens allergic cases
**Key point:** Allergic TIPS maps with CO2 venography.
items.kp: Contrast-allergic TIPS uses CO2 wedge mapping.

items.q: A 67-year-old man has a portal bifurcation puncture with the needle entering exactly at the fork. Flow splits beautifully into both lobes. Which bifurcation-target logic best explains aiming for portal forks in TIPS punctures?
o: Forks split flow evenly into both lobes
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Forks split flow evenly into both lobes.** Bifurcation landings feed right and left alike where branch sticks starve one side.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Forks share rather than block
- C: Targets govern lobar fate
- D: Lobar balance matters
**Key point:** TIPS punctures target portal bifurcations.
items.kp: Portal bifurcations make ideal TIPS targets.

items.q: A 55-year-old woman has extrahepatic portal puncture with free bleeding into the abdomen. The team tamponades with a covered stent urgently. Which extrahepatic lesson best keeps punctures inside liver capsules?
o: Intrahepatic targets bleed controllably unlike free abdomens
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Intrahepatic targets bleed controllably unlike free abdomens.** Liver tissue tamponades needle paths where free peritoneal sticks bleed unchecked.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Extrahepatic bleeds freely
- C: Abdomens fill catastrophically
- D: Livers tamponade tracts
**Key point:** TIPS stays intrahepatic under imaging.
items.kp: TIPS punctures stay intrahepatic to bleed controllably.

items.q: A 60-year-old man has his TIPS gradient rechecked at 15 mmHg with ongoing oozing despite an open shunt. The operator dilates further to 9 mmHg with control. Which recheck logic best drives further dilatation when gradients stay high?
o: Numbers with bleeding guide further opening
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Numbers with bleeding guide further opening.** Persistent hypertension with bleeding proves under-dilatation where further balloons finish the job.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Rechecks catch under-opening
- C: Oozing mirrors pressure
- D: Numbers govern shunts
**Key point:** High gradients with bleeding dilate further.
items.kp: Persistent high gradients with bleeding need further dilatation.

items.q: A 58-year-old woman has right upper quadrant pain with a small subcapsular haematoma after TIPS, stable with no blush. The team watches with repeat scans. Which contained-injury logic best watches stable subcapsular haematomas without blushes?
o: Tamponaded livers heal small contained bleeds alone
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Tamponaded livers heal small contained bleeds alone.** Capsule pressure contains small leaks where repeat scans confirm resolution.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Surgery suits uncontained bleeds
- C: Scans confirm resolution
- D: Pain follows punctures
**Key point:** Small contained haematomas watch with scans.
items.kp: Stable subcapsular haematomas watch with repeat scans.

items.q: A 64-year-old man has a TIPS placed for bleeding with coronary vein coils alongside. His follow-up endoscopy shows vanished varices. Which combined-success logic best credits shunts with coils for vanished varices?
o: Pressure drops with direct closure erase varices together
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Pressure drops with direct closure erase varices together.** Decompression shrinks channels where coils finish bleeding points, erasing varices jointly.

- B: Varices persist without treatment
- C: Coils miss pressure drivers
- D: Shunts miss some channels
**Key point:** Shunt-coil combinations erase varices.

items.q: A 52-year-old woman has her TIPS duplex showing brisk shunt flow with normalised portal direction and resolved ascites. The team spaces surveillance to six months. Which good-function logic best spaces scans when shunts work beautifully?
o: Working shunts earn wider surveillance intervals
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Working shunts earn wider surveillance intervals.** Normalised flow with dry abdomens proves function where frequent scans waste resources.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Daily scans waste resources
- C: Dry abdomens prove function
- D: Intervals widen with health
**Key point:** Working shunts space surveillance out.
items.kp: Well-functioning shunts earn wider surveillance intervals.

items.q: A 66-year-old man has a stenosed TIPS revised with angioplasty and an extended covered stent. His gradient normalises. Which revision logic best explains relining stenosed shunts with covered extensions?
o: Fresh lining bars the hyperplasia that choked old metal
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Fresh lining bars the hyperplasia that choked old metal.** Tissue ingrowth narrows old tracts where new fabric walls it off durably.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Stenoses recur without lining
- C: Bare invites repeat ingrowth
- D: Gradients prove revisions
**Key point:** Stenosed shunts reline with covered extensions.
items.kp: Stenosed TIPS revise with covered relining.

items.q: A 59-year-old woman has lifelong hepatology follow-up booked after TIPS with cancer surveillance and bone health checks. She asks why livers still need watching. Which palliation logic best explains lifelong follow-up since shunts never cure cirrhosis?
o: Shunts relieve pressure while livers still fail and seed tumours
Bones never weaken with liver disease
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Shunts relieve pressure while livers still fail and seed tumours.** Diversion eases plumbing where parenchyma keeps scarring and screening catches cancers.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Shunts palliate rather than cure
- C: Cancers haunt cirrhosis
- D: Bones thin with cholestasis
**Key point:** Shunted livers need lifelong watching.
items.kp: Shunted cirrhotic livers need lifelong follow-up.
